title: A study to assess the effect and safety of efgartigimod IV in participants from 12 years to less than 18 years of age with chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
official: ARGX-113-2409: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blinded, Parallel-Arm, Placebo- Controlled, Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Study Followed by an Open-Label Arm to Evaluate Efgartigimod IV in Pediatric Participants from 12 Years to Less Than 18 Years of Age with Chronic ITP
summary: Main objective: To confirm an appropriate dose of efgartigimod IV in participants with chronic ITP in the DBTP
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1A.  Is aged 12 to <18 years when completing the informed consent process, defined as providing informed assent according to local regulations and having a parent or guardian sign the ICF. Participants who are at the age of majority, according to local regulations, may sign the ICF
2. 10) Has documented baseline mean platelet count of <30 × 109/L before randomization on study day 1
3. 11) Has 1 documented qualifying platelet count (ie, a platelet count used in the formula for calculating the arithmetic mean) on study day 1 before randomization
4. 12) Has at least 2 documented qualifying platelet counts between study day −14 and study day 1 before randomization
5. 13) Has at least 3 documented qualifying platelet counts in the 3 months before randomization on study day 1
6. 14) Has no documented platelet count of >35 × 109/L within 30 days before randomization on study day 1
7. 2A. Is capable of completing the informed consent process as described in Section 10.1.3, and can comply with protocol requirements
8. 3) If an FAOCBP (defined in Section 10.4.1.1), agrees to use contraceptive measures consistent with local regulations and study requirements defined in Section 10.4.2.1
9. 4) If an FAOCBP, has a negative serum pregnancy test at screening and a negative urine pregnancy test at baseline before receiving IMP (Section 10.4.2.1)
10. 5) Has a documented diagnosis of primary ITP, as defined by the IWG1,3: a platelet count of <100 × 109 /L in the absence of other causes or disorders that may be associated with thrombocytopenia
11. 6A. Has a documented duration of primary ITP of more than 12 months on the date the informed consent process is complete
12. 7) Has documented prior ITP treatment with at least 1 of the following: corticosteroids, IVIg, anti-D immunoglobulin (for participants who are nonsplenectomized and Rho[D]-positive), TPO-RAs, or rituximab
13. 8) Has documented prior response, defined as 1 platelet count of ≥50 × 109 /L to at least 1 of the following ITP treatments: prednisone, other or nonspecified corticosteroids, IVIg, or anti-D immunoglobulin (for participants who are  nonsplenectomized and Rho[D]-positive)
14. 9) Has documented insufficient response to a prior ITP treatment with corticosteroids, IVIg,anti-D immunoglobulin (for participants who are nonsplenectomized and Rho[D]-positive), TPO-RAs, rituximab, or splenectomy, as defined by any of the following criteria:  a. No platelet count of ≥50 × 109/L after treatment  b. Platelet count of ≥50 × 109/L after treatment followed by platelet count <50 × 109/L  c. Less than 2-fold increase in platelet count from the pretreatment count d. No platelet count of ≥30 × 109/L after splenectomy  e. Platelet count of ≥30 × 109/L after splenectomy followed by platelet count <30 × 109/L  f. Reduction in platelet count to <30 × 109/L if tapering corticosteroids  g. Ongoing need for continuous prednisone (or corticosteroid equivalent) 5 mg/day to maintain a platelet count of ≥30 × 109 /L and/or to avoid bleeding  h. Repeated corticosteroid administration for at least 2 months to maintain a platelet count of ≥30 × 109/L and/or to avoid bleeding
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1) Besides the indication under study, known autoimmune disease or any medical condition that would interfere with an accurate assessment of clinical symptoms of chronic ITP or puts the participant at undue risk
2. 10) Different IMP received in another clinical study <12 weeks or <5 half-lives (whichever is longer) before screening
3. 11) Anti-CD20 or anti-CD19 antibody received <6 months before screening
4. 12) IVIg, SCIg, or PLEX received <3 weeks before screening
5. 13) Live or live-attenuated vaccine received <4 weeks before treatment
6. 14) Prior ITP therapy not discontinued per the defined washout period (refer to Table 10)
7. 15) Secondary ITP according to the following definition by the IWG1: all forms of immune-mediated thrombocytopenia except primary ITP
8. 16) Documented prior arterial or venous thrombosis within 12 months before screening
9. 17) Concurrent ITP therapy, except as specified in this protocol (refer to Section 6.9.3)
10. 18) Nonimmune thrombocytopenia
11. 19) History of hereditary thrombocytopenia
12. 2) Serious or severe active infection that is not sufficiently resolved in the investigator’s opinion
13. 20) ITP-associated critical or severe bleeding (refer to Table 12)
14. 21) Positive serum test result at screening for active infection with any of the following: a. HBV indicative of an acute or chronic infection unless associated with a negative HBV DNA test result b. HCV based on HCV antibody assay unless a negative RNA test result is available (Section 10.2.1.2) c. HIV based on confirmed positive serology results (Section 10.2.1.3)
15. 22) At the screening visit, clinically significant laboratory abnormalities as follows: a. Hemoglobin concentration ≤9 g/dL b. Severe renal impairment with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2. eGFR will be calculated using the bedside Schwartz formula.  c. Aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase >3.0× the ULN d. Total serum bilirubin concentration >1.5× the ULN e. Total IgG level below the lower limit of normal
16. 23) History of malignancy unless considered cured by adequate treatment a. With no evidence of recurrence for ≥3 years before first IMP administration b. One of the following cancers: • Basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer • Carcinoma in situ of the cervix • Carcinoma in situ of the breast • Incidental histological findings of prostate cancer (TNM stage T1a or T1b)
17. 24) Modification of concurrent ITP therapy during the screening period
18. 25A. Occurrence of rescue ITP therapy during the screening period (from the date the informed consent process is complete to randomization)
19. 3A. Recent major surgery (within 3 months of screening) or intention to have major surgery during the study
20. 4) Current participation in another interventional clinical study
21. 5) Known hypersensitivity to IMP or 1 of its excipients
22. This criterion was removed in version 2.0
23. 7) Pregnant or lactating state or intention to become pregnant during the study
24. 8) Previous participation in an efgartigimod clinical study and at least 1 dose of IMP received
25. 9) Monoclonal antibody that is not an anti-CD20 or Fc-fusion protein received <4 weeks before screening
